## Connections across borders

Latin America has been important in shaping the relationships behind *RafikiArdhi*. It is where many connections were formed through shared interests, experiences, and a common commitment to understanding the environment. Although distance means we do not see one another as often as we would like, these relationships have continued to grow beyond the places and moments where they began.

![View from Sugarloaf, showing the city intertwine within the landscape.](../images/brazil-sugarloaf.jpg){fig-alt="View across Rio de Janeiro from Sugarloaf Mountain"}

Each city seems to be part of the environment, not an addition to it.

![Hidden amoung the chaos of the city there are places such as Parque Lage courtyard (left) and its gardens (right)](../images/brazil-hidden-city.jpg){fig-alt="The historic courtyard of Parque Lage on the left and its gardens on the right"}

## Working together, wherever we are

Good collaborations are not defined by how often people meet, but by what they continue to build together. We remain connected through research projects, exchanging ideas and contributing our different experiences and perspectives. These ongoing relationships are an important part of how *RafikiArdhi* works: international in its connections, collaborative in its approach, and focused on bringing people and knowledge together across borders.

![Working on the SteamBioAfrica project (2023) with our Brazilian partners we met in 2018 (Windhoek, Namibia)](../images/brazil-to-namib.jpg){fig-alt="Working with Brazilian partners in Namibia"}

Working with *[Soil Consultoria Socioambiental](https://soilconsultoriasocioambiental.com)*, one of our major partners, we have developed research and tools across several areas:

- **Pedological profile modelling:** Developing continuous soil profile models and making the methods accessible through our ([phySpline tool](tools.html#spline)) and ([published research](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2026.181621)).
- **Country-scale soil mapping:** Producing high-resolution predictions of soil types, extending the work described in our ([published research](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geodrs.2024.e00902)).
- **Refining continental soil maps:** Translating broad-scale soil information into more detailed local ([soil type maps](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geomat.2024.100028)).
- **Three-dimensional carbon mapping:** Calculating soil carbon stocks continuously through the soil profile, supported by our [carbon calculator](tools.html#carbon) and ([published research](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pedsph.2024.07.004)).

Together, these projects bring different expertise and perspectives into the same work. The result is more than any one of us could produce alone: a whole greater than the sum of its parts.
